body.heading: Listen to the start
paragraphs: Every word starts with a sound. Say 'sun' very slowly: sss-un. The first sound is sss. Say 'Mango': mmm-ango. Mango starts with mmm!
Grown-ups call this the beginning sound. Hearing it is the very first step to reading — before letters, before books, just ears.

body.heading: Think and talk
paragraphs: 1. What sound does YOUR name start with? Stretch it out: 'Bbb-ben!' Now do everyone in your family.
2. I spy something that starts with mmm. (It might be Mango… or a muffin… or Mom!)

takeaway: Every word begins with a sound — stretch the word slowly and the first sound pops out: sss-un, mmm-ango, bbb-all.
materials: Just you and this page — no materials needed
supervision: A grown-up nearby is recommended for younger readers; the think-and-talk questions work well read aloud together.
safetyNotes: Reading only — no physical activity or materials are involved.
